1124.body:
The key fact about "Spectacular Riches" is how its eight prize levels are built. The prize money leans no one direction in particular. Games built like this offer both kinds of prizes without favoring either. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

Every line of Spectacular Riches's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
1124.headline: How prizes are split

1125.body:
The top prize count on "$1,000,000 Black Titanium" has not moved for over a month. The game still has three of five top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

If "$1,000,000 Black Titanium" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
1125.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

1127.body:
"Triple Tripler" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $1,800 was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold nineteen of the original twenty. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

Everything above about "Triple Tripler" comes from the Ohio Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
1127.headline: The top prize list got shorter

1134.body:
"Crazy Cash" has 622,368 prizes of $1 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $100 prize, with 1,391 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If you play "Crazy Cash" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
1134.headline: Prize table details

1140.body:
"$25, $50 or $250" has 3,556 of 3,675 top prizes left and is early in its run. Only a small slice of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

The table below shows the full count for "$25, $50 or $250", with every prize level included.
1140.headline: Tickets sold so far

696.body:
"Monopoly 200X" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. Of its unclaimed prize money, about three-quarters is in wins under $10,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

Today's free summary of "Monopoly 200X" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
696.headline: The prize mix in this game

762.body:
The prize money on "Billion" leans toward small, frequent prizes. It is spread over nine prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $20 million. Games built like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

How far "Billion" is through its run does not decide anything by itself. It changes how closely to look at the other numbers.

The numbers for "Billion" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
762.headline: What type of game it is

827.body:
"50th Anniversary" has had no $15 million top prize claimed for over a month. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Every line of 50th Anniversary's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
